title: “Brahmin, if an elder is eighty, ninety, or a hundred years old, and he enjoys sensual pleasures, dwells amidst sensual pleasures, is burned by the…
content: “Brahmin, if an elder is eighty, ninety, or a hundred years old, and he enjoys sensual pleasures, dwells amidst sensual pleasures, is burned by the fever of sensual pleasures, consumed by sensual thoughts, and strives for sensual pleasures — such a person is called a fool, not an elder. But if a young person, brahmin, a youth with black hair, endowed with the blessing of youth, in the prime of life, does not enjoy sensual pleasures, does not dwell amidst sensual pleasures, is not burned by the fever of sensual pleasures, not consumed by sensual thoughts, and does not strive for sensual pleasures — such a person is called a wise one, an elder.”

title: “Truly, monks, it is impossible that one could enjoy sensual pleasures apart from sensual pleasures, apart from sensual perceptions, apart from sensual thoughts.”
content: “Truly, monks, it is impossible that one could enjoy sensual pleasures apart from sensual pleasures, apart from sensual perceptions, apart from sensual thoughts.”

title: “Ānanda, here a monk abides contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having restrained covetousness and sorrow in the world; abides contemplating…
content: “Ānanda, here a monk abides contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having restrained covetousness and sorrow in the world; abides contemplating feelings as feelings … mind as mind … phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having restrained covetousness and sorrow in the world. Ānanda, thus a monk is an island unto himself, a refuge unto himself, seeking no other refuge; with the Dhamma as his island, with the Dhamma as his refuge, seeking no other refuge.”

title: “Monks, if one does not intend, does not plan, and has no tendency towards anything, there is no basis for the establishment of consciousness. When…
content: “Monks, if one does not intend, does not plan, and has no tendency towards anything, there is no basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is no basis, consciousness does not become established. When consciousness is not established and does not grow, there is no descent of name-and-form. With the cessation of name-and-form, the six sense-bases cease … such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

title: “The stream of craving flows everywhere, The creeper of craving sprouts and stands. Seeing that creeper that has arisen, Cut its root with wisdom.” “People,…
content:
“The stream of craving flows everywhere,
The creeper of craving sprouts and stands.
Seeing that creeper that has arisen,
Cut its root with wisdom.”

“People, immersed in sensual pleasures,
Delight in various pleasures.
Though they seek happiness,
They undergo birth and aging.”

“People bound by craving,
Thrashing about, terrified,
Like hares caught in a snare —
Bound by craving,
They undergo suffering for a long time.”

“People bound by craving,
Thrashing about, terrified,
Like hares caught in a snare —
Therefore, a monk who desires his own dispassion
Should abandon craving.”

title: “Monks, just as a young man or woman, youthful, fond of adornment, would be distressed, ashamed, and disgusted if the carcass of a snake, a…
content: “Monks, just as a young man or woman, youthful, fond of adornment, would be distressed, ashamed, and disgusted if the carcass of a snake, a dog, or a human were hung around their neck; so too, monks, that monk, examining the peril in those thoughts … the mind becomes steadied, settled, unified, and concentrated.”

title: One with craving as companion Wanders for a long time — Now here, now there — He cannot stop The wandering of rebirth. Having understood…
content:
One with craving as companion
Wanders for a long time —
Now here, now there —
He cannot stop
The wandering of rebirth.
Having understood this danger —
That craving is the origin of suffering —
The monk, abandoning craving,
Not grasping, not clinging,
Mindfully dwells,
Living the homeless life.

title: Elder Kulla: Kulla went to the charnel ground, Saw a woman abandoned, Thrown away in the cemetery, Food for worms. “Kulla, look at this body…
content:
Elder Kulla:

Kulla went to the charnel ground,
Saw a woman abandoned,
Thrown away in the cemetery,
Food for worms.

“Kulla, look at this body —
Diseased, foul, stinking,
Oozing, seeping,
Delighting fools.”

Having taken up the mirror of Dhamma,
I attained right view.
I contemplated this body —
Empty inside and out.

As it is below, so above,
As above, so below,
As below, so above,
As above, so below.

As by day, so by night,
As by night, so by day,
As before, so after,
As after, so before.

Such a one does not delight
In the five kinds of music.
When one-pointed,
Rightly meditating on the Dhamma.

title: “Monks, these three are inner stains, inner enemies, inner foes, inner murderers, inner adversaries. What three? Greed, monks, is an inner stain, inner enemy, inner…
content: “Monks, these three are inner stains, inner enemies, inner foes, inner murderers, inner adversaries. What three? Greed, monks, is an inner stain, inner enemy, inner foe, inner murderer, inner adversary. Hatred, monks, is an inner stain … Delusion, monks, is an inner stain, inner enemy, inner foe, inner murderer, inner adversary. These, monks, are the three inner stains, inner enemies, inner foes, inner murderers, inner adversaries.”

title: “Monks, I will teach about suffering and the root of suffering. Listen … And what, monks, is suffering? Form, monks, is suffering; feeling is suffering;…
content: “Monks, I will teach about suffering and the root of suffering. Listen … And what, monks, is suffering? Form, monks, is suffering; feeling is suffering; perception is suffering; formations are suffering; consciousness is suffering. This, monks, is called suffering. And what, monks, is the root of suffering? It is this craving that leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and lust, delighting here and there — that is, craving for sensual pleasures, craving for existence, craving for non-existence.”
